summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests two PD-1-based immunotherapy regimens given before surgery (neoadjuvant) in patients with resectable stage IIIB to stage IV (M1a) melanoma, either cutaneous or of unknown primary. Patients are randomized to pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for two infusions, or to one infusion of ipilimumab (3 mg/kg) plus nivolumab (1 mg/kg), followed by one infusion of nivolumab 240 mg IV 3 weeks later; both arms then have lymph node dissection and no adjuvant treatment. The study measures overall survival at 24 months, and event-free survival at 12 months.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa dos regímenes de inmunoterapia basados en PD-1 administrados antes de la cirugía (neoadyuvantes) en pacientes con melanoma resecable en estadio IIIB a estadio IV (M1a), de origen cutáneo o de origen primario desconocido. Los pacientes se asignan al azar a pembrolizumab 200 mg por vía IV cada 3 semanas, en dos infusiones, o a una infusión de ipilimumab (3 mg/kg) más nivolumab (1 mg/kg), seguida de una infusión de nivolumab 240 mg por vía IV 3 semanas después; en ambos brazos se realiza luego la disección de ganglios linfáticos y no se da tratamiento adyuvante. El estudio mide la supervivencia global a 24 meses y la supervivencia libre de eventos a 12 meses.
who_for: Confirmed cutaneous melanoma or melanoma of unknown primary.
AJCC stage IIIB or IVa disease that is resectable and measurable by iRECIST criteria.
Adequate blood, kidney, liver, and heart function.
not_for: Prior treatment with PD-1 and CTLA-4 inhibitors.
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic disease-modifying or immunosuppressive drugs.
Any condition the investigator judges to place the patient at unacceptable risk, including conditions that would interfere with participation.
